title: screenshot / record_video write to any path the model chooses

evidence.quote: async ({ udid, output_path, type, display, mask }) => {

reason: output_path is only length-limited; absolute paths and '..' are accepted as-is, so a prompt-injected call can overwrite any file the user can write (e.g. ~/.zshrc, project sources, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys) with image/video bytes, and record_video's force flag overwrites existing files. Content is not attacker-chosen, so this is file destruction, not code execution. The '--' separator correctly prevents flag injection.
fix: Resolve the path (fs.realpath on the parent) and require it to stay inside an allowed output directory such as ~/Downloads (path.relative must not start with '..'), and refuse to overwrite existing files unless the user approves.

title: On-screen accessibility text of the simulated app is returned raw to the model
reason: ui_describe_all / ui_describe_point return all text visible in the app under test (which may show web content, chat messages or other third-party text) without marking it as untrusted; injected text there can steer the model's next ui_type / ui_tap / screenshot calls (see M001).
fix: Mark the returned accessibility tree as untrusted data in the tool result, and keep human approval for file-writing tools.

title: Command execution is hardened (execFile, no shell, '--', strict schemas)

evidence.quote: const { stdout, stderr } = await execFileAsync(cmd, args, { shell: false });

reason: Checked every tool that starts a process: commands run without a shell, udid is checked against a strict UUID regex, duration against a number regex, enum fields use z.enum, numbers are z.number, and free-text values come after '--'. No command or argument injection found.
